cards.text: The writer of Hebrews has spent this whole letter showing who Jesus is and what He has done. Now he turns to the people he calls brothers and starts with the word therefore. Friend, in a letter, therefore is the oven timer going off: something is READY.

cards.question: Because of Jesus, the writer says believers now have confidence to enter a holy place. Which one?
How do believers get that confidence to enter the Most Holy Place?
The writer calls it a new and living way, opened for us through a curtain. True or false: he says that curtain is the body of Jesus.

cards.text: A way that's already OPENED. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer waiting for somebody to pull the handle, and here nobody's waiting on any handle at all.

cards.question: The writer adds that believers have a great ___ over the house of God.
The way in is open, and the great priest is over the house of God. So what does the writer tell them to do?

cards.text: And he says how to come: with a sincere heart, in full assurance of faith. Not hovering in the doorway like a guy who isn't sure he's at the right party.

cards.question: The writer says their hearts have been sprinkled clean. Clean of what?
True or false: the writer also says their bodies have been washed with pure water.

cards.text: Next, he tells them to hold on to the hope they profess. Not loosely, either. RESOLUTELY.

cards.question: Why can they hold on to the hope they profess so tightly?

cards.text: Then the writer turns their eyes from themselves to each other. He tells them to think about how to spur one another on.

cards.question: The writer wants them to spur one another on. Toward what?

cards.text: A spur isn't a polite little tap on the shoulder. It's the friend in the group chat who texts, "You said gym today. I can SEE your location."

cards.question: The writer warns about something some of them had made a habit of. What was it?
True or false: the writer says to encourage one another less as they see the Day approaching.

cards.text: Encourage each other all the more as you see the Day approaching, he says. I don't know when that Day comes, friend, so I keep these ovens WARM.

Now the writer's tone changes, and he talks about someone who deliberately goes on sinning after receiving the knowledge of the truth. Friend, this is the part where you set the cookie down and sit up straight.

cards.question: For someone who deliberately keeps on sinning after knowing the truth, what does the writer say no longer remains?
True or false: the writer says all that's left for that person is a fearful expectation of judgment.

cards.text: Then he looks back to the law of Moses, and to anyone who rejected it.

cards.question: What happened to someone who rejected the law of Moses, on the testimony of two or three witnesses?

cards.text: Then comes a hard question. If that was so under Moses, how much more severely does someone deserve to be punished who has trampled on the Son of God?

cards.question: The writer says that same person has profaned the ___ of the covenant and insulted the ___ of grace.

cards.text: The writer reminds them that they know the One who said, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay,” and again, “The Lord will judge His people.”

cards.question: So what does the writer call falling into the hands of the living God?

cards.text: Then the writer changes gears and tells them to remember their early days in the light. Friend, after years in a junk drawer, one crack of kitchen light had me waving my mustache like a game show contestant.

cards.question: What did they endure back in those early days in the light?

answers.text: A great conflict in the face of suffering
A long famine across the whole land
A hard march through the desert

cards.question: True or false: sometimes they were publicly exposed to ridicule and persecution, and other times they were partners with people treated that way.

cards.text: They sympathized with those in prison. And then their own property was confiscated.

cards.question: How did they accept the confiscation of their property?
Why could they take losing their property with joy?

answers.text: They had a better and permanent possession
They expected to get it all back soon
They never cared much about their things

cards.text: They lost their stuff JOYFULLY, and I lost one spot on a kitchen counter and moped in a drawer like it was my JOB. So the writer says, don't throw away your confidence.

cards.question: Why hold on to that confidence? What does the writer say it holds?
The writer tells them they need to ___, so that after they have done the will of God, they will receive what He has promised.

cards.text: Then the writer quotes Scripture, with God speaking: “In just a little while, He who is coming will come and will not delay.”

cards.question: In that same quote, God says His righteous one will live by what?
True or false: God says He takes pleasure in the one who shrinks back.
So which group does the writer say he and his readers belong to?

answers.text: Those who have faith and preserve their souls
Those who shrink back and are destroyed
Those still deciding which way to go

findings.problem: The opening card states a fact from outside the passage with no reference: that the writer has spent the whole letter showing who Jesus is and what He has done (Hebrews 1-10). The card cites only Hebrews 10:19, so its citation doesn't cover what it tells.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question opens with "Because of Jesus," which gives away the answer to card 3 ("By the blood of Jesus"). Once Jesus is named as the reason, the wrong answers on card 3 (the law of Moses, their own good works) are ruled out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats Hebrews 10:20, which card 4 already covered, and then adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage. The joke should ride along on a card that moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The right answer, "He who promised is faithful," is the passage's exact wording and sounds like the Bible. The wrong answers ("They have earned it themselves" and "Their leaders told them so") sound plain and modern, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This is a joke-only story card. It explains the word "spur" again, but card 14 already covered Hebrews 10:24. It tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The question says "some of them" had made a habit of neglecting meeting together. Hebrews 10:25 says only "as some have made a habit." It doesn't say those people were among the readers.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This card restates "encourage each other all the more as you see the Day approaching," which card 17 just answered, and then adds a joke. It's a recap card and doesn't move the passage forward.

The card says the writer "talks about someone who deliberately goes on sinning." Hebrews 10:26 says "If we deliberately go on sinning." The writer includes himself and his readers, and the card turns that into an outside "someone." Card 8 does the same thing, turning "we know Him" into "they know."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The second half of Hebrews 10:27, "and of raging fire that will consume all adversaries," is never told on any card. The baker leaves without this detail of the warning.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new drawer moment: Papa Dorin "waving my mustache like a game show contestant" at the light. His backstory says the light was bittersweet and everyone held their breath, and jokes may only make up small moments around his bakery. The joke is also a pun on "light." The core of Hebrews 10:32 is remembering how they endured suffering, and the comparison is excitement, which is a different action.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: "And then their own property was confiscated" adds an order of events. Hebrews 10:34 lists sympathizing with prisoners and the confiscation side by side and doesn't say which came first.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card says the writer "quotes Scripture," which is a fact from outside the passage (Habakkuk 2:3-4), but it gives no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.
